Make, read and verify an identity card for your signing key

Source: R/idcard.R
idcrd.Rd

An identity card ties your public signing key to who you are: your name and, if you give them, your ORCID iD, e-mail address, web page and affiliation, all signed with the key itself. Publish the card (on your web page, in a repository, beside a paper) and give its fingerprint somewhere people already know you by (the paper, your ORCID record, a talk). Anyone can then check with idcrdvrf() that the card is intact and in date, that its fingerprint is the one you gave, and that an attestation or a bundle was signed by the key it carries.

idcrd() makes a card from a key of fipskg() (ML-DSA or SLH-DSA) or pqckg() (XMSS; making the card uses one of the key's signatures). idcrdrd() reads a card written with file. idcrdvrf() checks one.

Usage

idcrd(
  key,
  name,
  orcid = NULL,
  email = NULL,
  url = NULL,
  affil = NULL,
  days = 730,
  file = NULL
)

idcrdrd(path)

idcrdvrf(card, fpr = NULL, at = Sys.time(), atst = NULL)

Arguments

key

Your private signing key, from fipskg() or pqckg().

name

Your name as you want it shown, one string.

orcid, email, url, affil

Optional, one string each: your ORCID iD ("0000-0002-1825-0097", or its https://orcid.org/ address), e-mail address, web page (https://) and affiliation.

days

How many days the card is valid for, from now. Default 730.

file

Optional path to write the card to, as JSON.

path

The path of a card file written by idcrd().

card

A card, from idcrd() or idcrdrd(), or the path of one.

fpr

Optional: the fingerprint you were given for this person, with or without its spaces. Without it the card is checked only against itself.

at

The time to check the card's dates at: a POSIXct or anything as.POSIXct() reads, taken as UTC. Defaults to now.

atst

Optional: an attestation of cpsatst(), or a bundle of cpsbndl() or cpsbndlrd(), to check was signed by the card's key. Check the attestation itself with cpschkatst() or cpsbndlvrf().

Value

idcrd() and idcrdrd(): a list of class rmbl_id_card with the card's fields (type, version, name, orcid, email, url, affil, scheme, public, context, prehash, issued_utc, expires_utc, signature) and its fingerprint; idcrd() returns it invisibly when it writes file. idcrdvrf(): a list of class rmbl_id_check with ok, checks (a data frame with check, ok and detail), fingerprint and card. print() shows a summary.

Details

A card is self-signed. Its signature proves that the card was made by whoever holds the private key and that nothing in it has changed since; it cannot prove that the name on it is true. That is what the fingerprint is for: a card whose fingerprint matches the one you published where people know you is the key you meant. The card's signature is made under its own context string (or, for XMSS, over a payload naming the card type), so it can never be passed off as an attestation, nor an attestation as a card.

The fingerprint is the SHA-256 digest of the scheme and the public key, written as 16 groups of four hexadecimal digits; compare all of it. An ORCID iD is checked against its check digit (ISO 7064 MOD 11-2), an e-mail address for its shape and a web page for an https:// address.

idcrdvrf() records every step as a row of checks: card_complete, card_type, signature, in_date (at at), and orcid when the card has one, fingerprint when fpr is given, signed_by_card when atst is given. ok is TRUE only when every row passed; a failed check is a row, not an error.

Errors: key not a private key of fipskg() or pqckg(); name not one non-empty string; an optional field that is not one string, an ORCID iD with a wrong check digit, an e-mail address or a web page of the wrong shape; days not a positive whole number; path not a card file.

See also

fipskg(), pqckg(), cpsatst(), cpschkatst(), cpsbndlvrf().

Examples

# once: make a key and a card, publish the card, give out the fingerprint
key <- fipskg("ML-DSA-44")
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
idcrd(
  key,
  "Ada Lovelace",
  orcid = "0000-0002-1825-0097",
  url = "https://example.org/ada",
  file = f
)
card <- idcrdrd(f)
card
#> ╭── Identity card ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   name         Ada Lovelace                                                 │
#> │   orcid        0000-0002-1825-0097                                          │
#> │   web          https://example.org/ada                                      │
#> │   key          ML-DSA-44                                                    │
#> │   fingerprint  3006 6273 3775 DEDE F5C0 567C 92AB C399 BD9A CC28 D2AA 7F9B  │
#> │                7985 2F32 2311 6905                                          │
#> │   issued       2026-10-28T06:49:30Z                                         │
#> │   expires      2028-10-27T06:49:30Z                                         │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
card$fingerprint
#> [1] "3006 6273 3775 DEDE F5C0 567C 92AB C399 BD9A CC28 D2AA 7F9B 7985 2F32 2311 6905"

# anyone, later: is this the card I was told about, and did it sign this?
man <- mkmnf(list(project = "demo"), env = FALSE)
a <- cpsatst(man, key)
res <- idcrdvrf(f, fpr = card$fingerprint, atst = a)
res$ok
#> [1] TRUE
res$checks
#>            check   ok
#> 1  card_complete TRUE
#> 2      card_type TRUE
#> 3      signature TRUE
#> 4        in_date TRUE
#> 5          orcid TRUE
#> 6    fingerprint TRUE
#> 7 signed_by_card TRUE
#>                                                                                detail
#> 1                                                                                    
#> 2                                 an rmbl identity card, signed under its own context
#> 3                               made by the holder of the card's key; unchanged since
#> 4 valid 2026-10-28T06:49:30Z to 2028-10-27T06:49:30Z; checked at 2026-10-28T06:49:30Z
#> 5                                                                 0000-0002-1825-0097
#> 6                                            the card's key is the one you were given
#> 7                                              the attestation carries the card's key

# a card edited after signing fails
bad <- card
bad$name <- "Someone Else"
idcrdvrf(bad)$ok
#> [1] FALSE

# an attestation made with another key is not the card's
other <- cpsatst(man, fipskg("ML-DSA-44"))
idcrdvrf(card, atst = other)$ok
#> [1] FALSE

# an ORCID iD with a wrong check digit is refused
try(idcrd(key, "Ada Lovelace", orcid = "0000-0002-1825-0098"))
#> Error : idcrd: `orcid` 0000-0002-1825-0098 has a wrong check digit
